87238.q: In undisturbed deposits, which layer is normally the oldest?
87238.e: New layers always settle on top of older ones. So the oldest layer is at the bottom, as long as the layers have not been folded or turned over.
87238.m: In undisturbed layers, the oldest is at the very bottom.

87239.q: Why is the Rhône much clearer where it leaves Lake Geneva in Geneva than where it flows into the lake?
a: The suspended particles have settled in the lake
Water is filtered in the lake
Geneva adds chemicals to the water
87239.e: The Rhône brings cloudy glacier water with a lot of fine rock material. In the calm lake these particles sink, and the water flows on clear.
87239.m: Lakes act like settling tanks for rivers’ suspended particles.

87240.q: In the long run, what happens to a lake into which rivers keep depositing material?
87240.e: The deposits make the lake shallower and smaller. Over thousands of years it can turn completely into land, for example into a marsh or a plain.
87240.m: Over time, lakes silt up because of deposits.

87241.q: What is volcanic tuff made of?
87241.e: Ash and small fragments thrown out during an eruption are deposited. When they harden, the rock tuff forms.
87241.m: Volcanic tuff is made of hardened volcanic ash.

87242.q: What has to happen for volcanic tuff to form?
a: A volcano must throw out a lot of ash
87242.e: During an eruption, ash and small fragments fall to the ground in thick layers. Over time they harden into tuff.
87242.m: Tuff forms from the ash of volcanic eruptions.

87243.q: In which country is Cappadocia, with its rock towers and cave homes made of tuff?
87243.e: In Cappadocia, erosion has shaped the soft tuff into rock towers. People have carved homes, churches and whole underground cities into them.
87243.m: Cappadocia in Turkey is famous for its tuff landscape.

87244.q: On which island do the giant stone figures called moai, made of tuff, stand?
87244.e: The people of Easter Island in the Pacific carved the statues out of volcanic tuff. It was easy to work with stone tools.
87244.m: The moai of Easter Island are mostly made of tuff.

87245.q: Why was tuff popular as a building stone from early times?
a: It is light and easy to work
87245.e: Tuff is porous, light and usually quite soft. It can be sawn and shaped with simple tools, and it insulates well.
87245.m: Tuff is light and easy to work.

a: Lime comes out of spring water, often around moss
87246.e: Lime-rich spring water gives off carbon dioxide in the air, and lime comes out of it. It coats mosses and plants and forms a porous rock.
87246.m: Tufa forms from lime deposited from spring water.

87247.q: Why is tufa often full of small holes and tubes?
a: The lime coated plants that later rotted
Gas bubbles from lava were trapped in it
The wind made holes in it
87247.e: As it forms, the lime coats mosses, stalks and leaves. When these plant parts decay, hollow spaces are left behind.
87247.m: The holes in tufa come from rotted plants.

87248.q: Why is there a lot of tuff around Rome?
a: There used to be many volcanoes there
There used to be a glacier there
There are many salt lakes there
87248.e: Rome lies in an area with many old volcanoes. Their ash formed thick layers of tuff, which the Romans used to build walls and houses.
87248.m: There is tuff around Rome because volcanoes used to be active there.

87249.q: In the shell model, what is the maximum number of electrons in the innermost shell (K shell)?
87249.e: The K shell is closest to the nucleus and is the smallest. It holds at most two electrons.
87249.m: The innermost shell holds at most two electrons.

87250.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that fit in the fourth shell (N shell)?
87250.e: With n = 4: 2 · 4² = 2 · 16 = 32. So the N shell can hold up to 32 electrons.
87250.m: The N shell holds at most 32 electrons.

87251.q: Which formula tells you the maximum number of electrons that fit in the nth shell?
87251.e: The maximum number of electrons in a shell is 2n², where n is the number of the shell. The formula applies to the inner shells up to the fourth.
87251.m: The nth shell holds at most 2n² electrons.

87252.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that fit in the third shell (M shell)?
87252.e: With n = 3: 2 · 3² = 2 · 9 = 18. So the M shell holds at most 18 electrons.
87252.m: The M shell can hold up to 18 electrons.

87253.q: What is the innermost electron shell called in the shell model?
87253.e: The shells are labelled K, L, M, N and so on from the inside out. The K shell is the first.
87253.m: From the inside out, the shells are called K, L, M and N.

87254.q: Where are the electrons in the shell model?
a: In the middle of the nucleus
Between protons and neutrons in the nucleus
87254.e: In the shell model, protons and neutrons sit in the nucleus. The electrons move on shells around the nucleus.
87254.m: Electrons move on shells around the nucleus.

87255.q: How many shells are occupied in a sodium atom with 11 electrons?
87255.e: The 11 electrons are arranged like this: 2 on the first, 8 on the second and 1 on the third shell.
87255.m: A sodium atom has three occupied shells.

87256.q: How are the 13 electrons of an aluminium atom arranged on the shells (from the inside out)?
87256.e: First the first shell is filled with 2 electrons, then the second with 8. The remaining 3 electrons go on the third shell.
87256.m: Shells are filled from the inside out.

87257.q: What must an electron take in to move to a shell further out?
87257.e: Outer shells have higher energy. An electron only jumps outwards if it takes in energy, for example from heat or light.
87257.m: An electron needs energy to jump to an outer shell.

87258.q: How many valence electrons does an argon atom with 18 electrons have?
87258.e: The 18 electrons are arranged as 2, 8 and 8. So there are 8 electrons on the outermost shell.

87259.q: How many valence electrons does a carbon atom have?
87259.e: Carbon has 6 electrons: 2 on the first and 4 on the second shell. The 4 outer ones are the valence electrons.

87260.q: How many valence electrons does an oxygen atom have?
87260.e: Oxygen has 8 electrons, arranged as 2 and 6. So there are 6 electrons on the outermost shell.

87261.q: How many valence electrons does a nitrogen atom have?
87261.e: Nitrogen has 7 electrons, arranged as 2 and 5. The outer shell carries 5 electrons.

87262.q: What is the rule called by which many atoms aim to have eight electrons in their outer shell?
87262.e: ‘Octet’ comes from the Latin word for eight. With eight outer electrons, an atom is especially stable.
87262.m: The octet rule says that atoms aim for eight outer electrons.

87263.q: How are valence electrons shown in Lewis notation?
a: As dots around the element symbol
As a number under the symbol
87263.e: In Lewis notation, each valence electron is a dot next to the element symbol. A pair of electrons can also be drawn as a line.
87263.m: In Lewis notation, dots show the valence electrons.

87264.q: How many valence electrons does a chlorine atom have?
87264.e: Chlorine has 17 electrons, arranged as 2, 8 and 7. So it is only one electron short of a full outer shell.

87265.q: How many valence electrons does a phosphorus atom with 15 electrons have?
87265.e: The 15 electrons are arranged as 2, 8 and 5. So there are 5 electrons on the outermost shell.

87267.q: Which element has the atomic number 20?
87267.e: Calcium has 20 protons in its nucleus. It comes straight after potassium in the periodic table.

87268.q: Which element has the atomic number 10?
87268.e: Neon has 10 protons in its nucleus. Fluorine has 9, sodium 11 and argon 18.

87269.q: What is the atomic number of sulphur?
87269.e: Sulphur has 16 protons in its nucleus. The number 32 is the mass number of the most common sulphur isotope.

87270.q: How are the elements arranged in the periodic table?
a: By the year they were discovered
87270.e: The elements are arranged by the number of protons in the nucleus, that is, by atomic number. Hydrogen, with 1, comes first.
87270.m: The periodic table is arranged by atomic number.

87271.q: Two atoms have the same atomic number. What is true of them?
a: They belong to the same element
They have different numbers of protons
87271.e: The atomic number shows the number of protons. The same number of protons means the same element, even if the number of neutrons can differ.
87271.m: The same atomic number means the same element.

87272.q: How many electrons does an electrically neutral atom with the atomic number 12 have?
87272.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons. With the atomic number 12, that makes 12 electrons.
87272.m: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons.

87273.q: Sodium has the atomic number 11. How many protons does a sodium atom have?
87273.e: The atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus. The number 23 is the mass number, which counts protons and neutrons together.
87273.m: The atomic number tells you the number of protons.

87274.q: How many main groups does the periodic table have in the classic layout?
87274.e: In the classic school numbering there are 8 main groups. Today IUPAC counts 18 groups in total, which also include the transition groups.
87274.m: In the classic layout, the periodic table has eight main groups.

87275.q: Which element is in the same main group as oxygen?
87275.e: Oxygen and sulphur are one below the other in main group 6. Both have six outer electrons.
87275.m: Oxygen and sulphur belong to main group 6.

87276.q: Which main group is also called the carbon group?
87276.e: The group is named after its first element. It also includes the metals tin and lead.
87276.m: The carbon group is main group 4.

87277.q: Which main group is aluminium in?
87277.e: Aluminium has 13 electrons, 3 of them on the outermost shell. It is the most common metal in the Earth's crust.

87278.q: How are the main groups arranged in the periodic table?
87278.e: Each main group forms a vertical column. Elements in the same column have similar chemical properties.
87278.m: Main groups run from top to bottom in the periodic table.

87279.q: What do the elements of the same main group have in common?
a: The same number of valence electrons
The same number of electron shells
87279.e: Elements in a main group have the same number of outer electrons. That is why they react in similar ways.
87279.m: Same main group means the same number of outer electrons.

87280.q: Which element is directly below carbon in the periodic table?
87280.e: Silicon comes directly after carbon in the same column. It is important for computer chips and solar cells.

87281.q: What is main group 3 also called, after its first element?
87281.e: The first element of main group 3 is boron. That is why it is called the boron group.
87281.m: Main group 3 is also called the boron group.

87282.q: From the second period on, which group of elements does each period start with on the far left?
87282.e: On the far left there is always an element with just one electron on the new outermost shell. These are the alkali metals such as lithium or sodium.
87282.m: From the second period on, every period starts with an alkali metal.

87283.q: What does the number of the period tell you?
a: The number of occupied electron shells
87283.e: All atoms in a period have the same number of electron shells. In period 2, for example, there are two shells.
87283.m: The period number shows the number of shells.

87284.q: How many elements are in the first period?
87284.e: The first period contains only hydrogen and helium. After that, the second period begins with lithium.
87284.m: The first period has only two elements.

87285.q: How many elements are in the second period?
87285.e: The second period runs from lithium to neon. That is 8 elements.
87285.m: The second period has eight elements.

87286.q: How many periods does today's periodic table have?
87286.e: The periodic table has 7 periods. Since 2016 the seventh period has been fully named, up to element 118.
87286.m: The periodic table has seven periods.

87287.e: Potassium has 19 electrons on four shells (2, 8, 8, 1). It opens period 4.
87287.m: Potassium is at the start of period 4.

87288.q: How does the atomic radius change across a period from left to right?
87288.e: Moving to the right, more protons are added but no new shell. The nucleus attracts the electrons more strongly, so the atoms get smaller.
87288.m: Within a period, atoms get smaller towards the right.

87289.q: Which group of elements does each period end with on the far right?
87289.e: At the end of each period the outermost shell is full. That is true of the noble gases.
87289.m: Every period ends with a noble gas.

87290.q: Which of these metals is an alkali metal?
87290.e: Sodium is in main group 1 and so it is an alkali metal. Calcium is an alkaline earth metal.

87291.q: Why is sodium kept under paraffin oil?
a: Because it reacts violently with air and water
87291.e: Sodium reacts with the oxygen and moisture in the air. The oil protects the metal from this.
87291.m: Alkali metals are kept under oil because they react with air and water.

87292.q: Which gas forms when sodium reacts with water?
87292.e: Sodium pushes the hydrogen out of the water. This makes hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide solution.
87292.m: Alkali metals form hydrogen gas with water.

87293.q: What is the solution like after an alkali metal has reacted with water?
87293.e: An alkaline solution forms, for example sodium hydroxide solution. Such solutions are basic, also called alkaline.
87293.m: Alkali metals form an alkaline solution with water.

87294.q: What flame colour does sodium produce?
87294.e: Sodium compounds turn a flame bright yellow. This flame colour is used to test for sodium.

87295.q: What flame colour does lithium produce?
87295.e: Lithium compounds turn a flame crimson. That is why they are also used in fireworks.

87296.q: Which metal has the lowest density of all metals?
87296.e: Lithium has a density of only about 0.53 g/cm³. It is so light that it would float on water.

87297.q: How hard is an alkali metal such as sodium?
a: You can cut it with a knife
You can only scratch it with diamond
It is as hard as steel
87297.e: Alkali metals are very soft. A freshly cut surface shines silvery but quickly tarnishes.
87297.m: Alkali metals are so soft you can cut them.

87298.q: How does the violence of the reaction with water change from lithium to caesium?
a: It increases at first, then decreases
87298.e: Going down the group, the atoms get bigger and the outer electron is given up more easily. That is why caesium reacts much more violently than lithium.
87298.m: Alkali metals react more and more violently going down the group.

87299.q: Which element is in main group 1 but is not an alkali metal?
87299.e: Like the alkali metals, hydrogen has one outer electron. But it is a non-metal and a gas.
87299.m: Hydrogen is in main group 1 but is not a metal.

87300.q: What does the word ‘halogen’ mean when translated?
87300.e: The word comes from Greek: ‘hals’ means salt and ‘gennan’ means to produce. Halogens form salts with metals.

87301.q: Which halogen is liquid at room temperature?
87301.e: Bromine is a reddish brown liquid. Apart from mercury, it is the only element that is liquid at room temperature.

87302.q: Which halogen is a solid, shiny greyish black substance at room temperature?
87302.e: Iodine forms greyish black, shiny crystals. When heated, it gives off a violet vapour.
87302.m: Iodine is solid at room temperature.

87303.q: Which main group are the halogens in?
87303.e: The halogens fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine are in main group 7, directly to the left of the noble gases.

87304.q: Which halogen is the most reactive?
87304.e: Fluorine is at the very top of the group and attracts electrons most strongly. It is the most reactive of all elements.
87304.m: Fluorine is the most reactive halogen.

87305.q: Which halogen is found as fluoride in many toothpastes?
87305.e: Fluoride hardens tooth enamel and so protects against tooth decay. That is why many toothpastes contain fluoride.
87305.m: Fluoride in toothpaste protects against tooth decay.

87306.q: Which acid forms when hydrogen chloride is dissolved in water?
87306.e: Hydrogen chloride (HCl) dissolves well in water. The solution is called hydrochloric acid; it is also found in stomach juice.
87306.m: Hydrogen chloride in water gives hydrochloric acid.

87307.q: Why is chlorine added to the water in a swimming pool?
a: To kill germs that cause disease
87307.e: Chlorine kills bacteria and other germs. That keeps the pool water hygienic.

87308.q: How many atoms make up a chlorine molecule?
87308.e: Chlorine exists as the molecule Cl₂. Two chlorine atoms share a pair of electrons.
87308.m: A chlorine molecule is made of two atoms.

87309.q: Why do noble gases hardly react with other substances?
87309.e: A full outer shell is very stable. So noble gases do not need to give up or take in electrons.
87309.m: Noble gases are unreactive because their outer shell is full.

87310.q: Which element has the lowest boiling point of all elements?
87310.e: Helium boils at about minus 269 °C, only a few degrees above absolute zero.
87310.m: Helium has the lowest boiling point of all elements.

87311.q: Which noble gas is used in very bright car headlights and flash lamps?
87311.e: In gas discharge lamps, xenon produces a very bright, almost white light. That is why they are called xenon headlights.
87311.m: Xenon gives very bright light in lamps.

87313.q: Which radioactive noble gas can get into cellars from the ground and is monitored by the Federal Office of Public Health?
87313.e: Radon forms when uranium in the ground decays. It can build up in houses especially in parts of the Alps and the Jura.
87313.m: Radon is a radioactive noble gas from the ground.

87314.q: How many valence electrons does a helium atom have?
87314.e: Helium has only 2 electrons, both on the first shell. That already makes this shell full.

87315.q: Which noble gas makes illuminated signs glow red?
87315.e: In a glass tube filled with neon, the gas glows red when electricity flows through it. That is where the word neon sign comes from.
87315.m: Neon glows red in sign tubes.

87316.q: Which noble gas is named after the Greek word for ‘hidden’?
87316.e: ‘Kryptos’ means hidden in Greek. Krypton is found in the air only in very small amounts.

87317.q: How many valence electrons do the alkaline earth metals have?
87317.e: Alkaline earth metals are in main group 2. So their outermost shell carries 2 electrons.
87317.m: Alkaline earth metals have two outer electrons.

87318.q: Which of these elements is an alkaline earth metal?
87318.e: Beryllium is the first element of main group 2. Lithium is an alkali metal, and boron and aluminium are not alkaline earth metals.
87318.m: Beryllium is the first alkaline earth metal.

87319.q: What are compounds of alkaline earth metals such as strontium and barium used for in fireworks?
a: So they can be stored longer
87319.e: Strontium compounds turn the flame red, barium compounds green. That creates the bright colours in fireworks.
87319.m: Alkaline earth metals give fireworks coloured flames.

87320.q: Which alkaline earth metal burns with a dazzling white light and was once used for flash photography?
87320.e: Magnesium burns with a very bright, white light. You must not look straight into it.
87320.m: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white light.

87321.q: Which radioactive alkaline earth metal did Marie and Pierre Curie discover in 1898?
87321.e: In 1898 the Curies discovered polonium and radium. Only radium belongs to main group 2.
87321.m: Radium is a radioactive alkaline earth metal.

87322.q: Which family of elements does calcium, found in bones and lime, belong to?
87322.e: Calcium is in main group 2 and so it is an alkaline earth metal. It is found in bones, teeth and limestone.
87322.m: Calcium is an alkaline earth metal.

87323.q: What substance is limestone, as found in the Jura, mainly made of?
87323.e: Limestone is mainly calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). It often formed from the shells of sea creatures.

87324.q: How violently does calcium react with water compared with sodium?
87324.e: Calcium reacts with water and forms hydrogen, but more calmly than sodium. Alkaline earth metals are less reactive than alkali metals.
87324.m: Alkaline earth metals react more calmly than alkali metals.

87325.q: What do all isotopes of an element have in common?
87325.e: Isotopes belong to the same element because they have the same number of protons in the nucleus. They differ only in the number of neutrons.
87325.m: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons.

87326.q: Which carbon isotope is used to find out the age of finds?
87326.e: Carbon-14 is radioactive and decays slowly, with a half-life of about 5730 years. This makes it possible to work out the age of wood or bones.
87326.m: Carbon-14 is used to date finds.

87327.q: How do isotopes of an element differ?
87327.e: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in the nucleus. That is why they have different weights.
87327.m: Isotopes differ in the number of neutrons.

87328.q: Which element is split in nuclear power stations to produce energy?
87328.e: In nuclear power stations, uranium nuclei are split by neutrons. This releases a lot of heat, which is used to make electricity.
87328.m: Uranium nuclei are split in nuclear power stations.

87329.q: Which is the most common carbon isotope in nature?
87329.e: Around 99 per cent of natural carbon is carbon-12. It has 6 protons and 6 neutrons.

87330.q: What does the Greek word ‘isotope’ mean when translated?
87330.e: Isotopes of an element are in the same place in the periodic table because they have the same number of protons.
87330.m: Isotopes are in the same place in the periodic table.

87331.q: What are isotopes called that decay and give off radiation?
87331.e: Radioactive isotopes have an unstable nucleus. When they decay, they give off radiation.
87331.m: Radioactive isotopes decay and give off radiation.

87332.q: How do isotopes of an element differ in their chemical behaviour?
a: Hardly at all, they react almost the same
Light isotopes do not react at all
87332.e: Chemical behaviour depends on the electrons. Isotopes have the same number of electrons, so they react almost the same.
87332.m: Isotopes of an element react almost the same chemically.

87333.q: What does the mass number of an atom tell you?
87333.e: The mass number counts all the particles in the nucleus. Electrons are very light and are not counted.
87333.m: The mass number is the sum of protons and neutrons.

87334.q: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
87334.e: You add the protons and neutrons together: 11 + 12 = 23.
87334.m: For the mass number, add protons and neutrons together.

87335.q: A fluorine atom has 9 protons and the mass number 19. How many neutrons does it have?
87335.e: Neutrons = mass number minus protons, so 19 minus 9 = 10.
87335.m: The number of neutrons is the mass number minus the number of protons.

87336.q: A chlorine atom has 17 protons and the mass number 35. How many neutrons does it have?
87336.e: You work out 35 minus 17 = 18. So the atom has 18 neutrons.
87336.m: Take the protons away from the mass number and you get the neutrons.

87337.q: Where is the mass number written next to the element symbol in nuclide notation?
87337.e: The mass number goes top left, the atomic number bottom left. Top right is used, for example, for the charge of an ion.
87337.m: The mass number is written top left of the symbol.

87338.q: Uranium-238 has 92 protons. How many neutrons does it have?
87338.e: You work out 238 minus 92 = 146. So an atom of uranium-238 has 146 neutrons.
87338.m: The number after the element name is the mass number.

87339.q: Why does the periodic table give chlorine an atomic mass of about 35.5 u instead of a whole number?
a: Because it is an average of its isotopes
Because a neutron is half as heavy
87339.e: Natural chlorine is about three quarters chlorine-35 and one quarter chlorine-37. The average is around 35.5 u.
87339.m: The atomic mass in the periodic table is an average of the isotopes.

87340.q: An atom has the mass number 27 and 14 neutrons. How many protons does it have?
87340.e: Protons = mass number minus neutrons, so 27 minus 14 = 13.
87340.m: You can work out the number of protons from the mass number and the number of neutrons.

87341.q: Which country did the chemist Dmitri Mendeleev come from?
87341.e: Mendeleev came from Tobolsk in Siberia. After a period of study in Heidelberg, he worked in St Petersburg.
87341.m: Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist.

87342.q: What did Dmitri Mendeleev draw up in 1869?
a: The periodic table of the elements
87342.e: Mendeleev arranged the elements known at the time in a table. This became the periodic table.
87342.m: Mendeleev drew up the periodic table in 1869.

87343.q: Mainly by which property did Mendeleev arrange the elements?
87343.e: Protons were still unknown at the time. Mendeleev arranged the elements by their atomic weight and by similar properties.
87343.m: Mendeleev arranged the elements by atomic mass.

87344.q: What did Mendeleev do when an element did not fit into his system?
a: He left gaps for unknown elements
He put it at the end
87344.e: Mendeleev left spaces and predicted the properties of the missing elements. Later these elements really were discovered.
87344.m: Mendeleev left gaps for elements not yet discovered.

87345.q: What became clear when the elements Mendeleev had predicted were discovered?
a: They did not fit into the system at all
They did not exist at all
87345.e: Mendeleev had predicted, for example, the mass and density of the missing elements. The measurements confirmed his predictions.

87346.q: How are the elements arranged in today's periodic table?
87346.e: Today the elements are arranged by atomic number. It gives the number of protons in the nucleus.
87346.m: The periodic table is arranged by the number of protons.

87347.q: Which chemical element was named in honour of Mendeleev?
87347.e: Mendelevium was made artificially in the USA in 1955. It has the atomic number 101.
87347.m: The element mendelevium bears Mendeleev's name.

87348.q: What are the vertical columns in the periodic table called?
87348.e: Elements in the same group have similar properties. The horizontal rows are called periods.
87348.m: The columns in the periodic table are called groups.

87349.q: What is a gearbox in a machine for?
87349.e: A gearbox transmits a rotation and changes its speed, torque or direction. This adapts the power of a motor to the task.
87349.m: A gearbox adjusts speed and torque.

87350.q: A small gear drives a large gear. How does the large gear turn?
a: More slowly, but with more force
87350.e: The large gear has more teeth. For one turn it needs several turns of the small gear, but it turns with more force.
87350.m: Small drives large: slower but stronger.

87351.q: What are cone-shaped gears used for?
a: To redirect a rotation round a corner
To turn a rotation into electricity
87351.e: With bevel gears the axles are usually at right angles to each other. So a rotation is turned through 90 degrees, for example in an angle grinder.
87351.m: Bevel gears turn a rotation round a corner.

87352.q: In which gear system does a screw engage with a gear wheel to give a very large reduction?
87352.e: The screw is called a worm. With a single-start worm, the worm wheel moves on by only one tooth per turn.
87352.m: A worm gear gives a very large reduction.

87353.q: Which gear system turns the rotation of the steering wheel into a sideways movement in many cars?
87353.e: A small gear at the end of the steering column engages with a toothed rack. When it turns, it pushes the rack left or right.
87353.m: Gear and rack turn rotation into pushing.

87354.q: What is the differential on a car's drive axle for?
a: Letting the wheels turn at different speeds on bends
87354.e: On a bend the outer wheel travels further than the inner one. The differential lets both driven wheels turn at different speeds anyway.
87354.m: The differential balances wheel speeds on bends.

87355.q: Two gears mesh directly with each other. Which way does the second gear turn?
87355.e: The teeth push each other along. If the first gear turns clockwise, the second turns anticlockwise.
87355.m: Meshing gears turn in opposite directions.

87356.q: What does an automatic gearbox in a car do differently from a manual one?
a: It only drives the front wheels
87356.e: With an automatic gearbox the vehicle chooses the right gear itself. There is no clutch pedal.
87356.m: An automatic gearbox changes gear by itself.

87357.q: A gear with 40 teeth drives a gear with 20 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn for one turn of the large one?
87357.e: In one turn the large gear moves 40 teeth along. The small gear needs 40 ÷ 20 = 2 turns for that.

87358.q: A gear with 12 teeth drives one with 36 teeth. What is the gear ratio (teeth of driven gear divided by teeth of driving gear)?
87358.e: You divide the teeth of the driven gear by the teeth of the driving gear: 36 ÷ 12 = 3.
87358.m: The gear ratio compares the teeth of the driven and driving gears.

87359.q: What does a reduction in a gearbox mean?
a: The output turns more slowly but with more force
The output turns faster and with more force
87359.e: With a reduction the speed drops, but the torque rises. You need this when pulling away, for example.
87359.m: A reduction makes things slower but stronger.

87360.q: A bike has a 48-tooth chainring at the front and a 16-tooth sprocket at the back. How many times does the back wheel turn for one turn of the pedals?
87360.e: The chain moves 48 teeth for each turn of the pedals. The sprocket turns 48 ÷ 16 = 3 times.
87360.m: A big chainring and a small sprocket make the bike fast.

87361.q: Which gear combination on a bike is best for steep mountain roads?
a: Small at the front, large at the back
Large at the front, small at the back
Large at the front, large at the back
Small at the front, small at the back
87361.e: A small chainring and a large sprocket give a big reduction. Pedalling is easier, but you go less far per turn.
87361.m: Uphill, choose small at the front and large at the back.

87362.q: A motor turns at 1500 revolutions per minute. A gearbox reduces it at a ratio of 3 to 1. How fast does the output turn?
87362.e: With a 3 to 1 reduction the output turns three times more slowly: 1500 ÷ 3 = 500.

87364.q: What effect does an idler gear between two gears have on the gear ratio?
a: None, it only changes the direction of rotation
87364.e: An idler gear simply passes the movement on. The ratio depends only on the first and last gear, but the direction of rotation is reversed.
87364.m: An idler gear only changes the direction of rotation.

87365.q: A gearbox has two stages with ratios of 2 and 3. What is the overall ratio?
87365.e: With several stages you multiply the individual ratios: 2 × 3 = 6.
87365.m: The ratios of several stages are multiplied.

87366.q: What is a ball bearing for?
a: It reduces friction on rotating shafts
87366.e: In a ball bearing, small balls roll between two rings. This lets a shaft turn easily and with little wear.
87366.m: Ball bearings let shafts turn easily.

87367.q: Which type of friction replaces sliding friction in a ball bearing?
87367.e: The balls roll between the rings instead of sliding. Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction.
87367.m: Ball bearings replace sliding with rolling.

87368.q: What is the part in a ball bearing called that keeps the balls evenly spaced?
87368.e: The cage makes sure the balls do not touch each other and stay evenly spread out.
87368.m: The cage keeps the balls in the bearing apart.

87369.q: For which vehicle were ball bearings used early on in the 19th century?
87369.e: As early as 1869 a Paris mechanic patented a ball bearing for bicycles. In the same year a bicycle with such bearings won a race from Paris to Rouen.
87369.m: Ball bearings were developed early for bicycles.

87370.q: What forces does a thrust bearing mainly take?
87370.e: “Axial” means in the direction of the axis. A thrust bearing withstands forces that push along the shaft.
87370.m: A thrust bearing carries forces along the shaft.

87371.q: What is a bearing called that has small cylinders instead of balls as rolling elements?
87371.e: Cylindrical rollers touch the rings along a line instead of at just one point. That is why they can carry bigger loads.
87371.m: Cylindrical roller bearings have rollers instead of balls.

87372.q: Which group of bearings do ball bearings belong to?
87372.e: In rolling bearings, balls or rollers roll between the rings. In plain bearings, by contrast, the shaft slides on a film of lubricant.

87373.q: Where on a bike do you find ball bearings?
87373.e: Ball bearings sit in the wheel hubs, the bottom bracket and the headset. That is where parts turn against each other.
87373.m: On a bike, wheels and pedals run on ball bearings.

87374.q: Why are ball bearings lubricated with grease?
a: To make them turn more slowly
87374.e: The grease forms a thin film between the balls and the rings. It reduces friction, protects against rust and keeps dirt out.
87374.m: Grease protects ball bearings from wear.

a: It turns the force of your hand into rotation
87375.e: A crank is a lever arm on a shaft. Turning the handle in a circle makes the shaft rotate.
87375.m: A crank is a lever that turns a shaft.

87376.q: Why do you need less force with a longer crank?
a: Because the lever arm is longer
87376.e: As with any lever: the longer the arm, the less force you need for the same turning effect.
87376.m: The longer the crank, the less force you need.

87377.q: What is the part of a bike called that the pedals are attached to?
87377.e: The crank arms sit on the left and right of the bottom bracket. You use them to drive the chainring.
87377.m: On a bike the pedals are fixed to the crank arms.

87378.q: Which engine part rotates because the pistons move up and down?
87378.e: The crankshaft has offset throws to which the pistons are connected by rods. This turns the up and down movement into rotation.
87378.m: The crankshaft turns piston strokes into rotation.

87379.q: What was the hand crank at the front of early cars used for?
87379.e: Before there were electric starters, you had to turn the engine over by hand. That was hard work and quite dangerous.
87379.m: Early cars were started with a crank.

87380.q: A crank handle is 0.5 m from the axle. Roughly how far does it travel in one turn?
87380.e: The handle moves on a circle with a radius of 0.5 m. The circumference is 2 × π × 0.5 m, so about 3.14 m.
87380.m: The crank handle moves in a circle round the axle.

87381.q: Which musical instrument plays music when you turn a crank?
87381.e: In a barrel organ the crank drives a bellows and a music roll. You often see them at fairs.
87381.m: A barrel organ is played with a crank.

87382.q: What is the crank on a winch for?
87382.e: When you turn the crank, the rope winds onto a drum. That way loads can be lifted or pulled.
87382.m: With the crank of a winch you wind up the rope.

87383.q: Which two parts of a combustion engine does the connecting rod join?
87383.e: The connecting rod transfers the force from the piston to the crankshaft. Without it the piston could not turn the shaft.
87383.m: The connecting rod joins piston and crankshaft.

87384.q: How does the lower end of the connecting rod, which sits on the crankshaft, move?
87384.e: The upper end follows the piston in a straight line. The lower end goes round in a circle with the crankshaft.
87384.m: The lower end of the connecting rod moves in a circle.

87385.q: What is the pin called that connects the connecting rod to the piston?
87385.e: The gudgeon pin passes crosswise through the piston and the small end of the connecting rod. This lets the rod swing relative to the piston.
87385.m: The gudgeon pin holds piston and connecting rod together.

87386.q: On a steam locomotive, what is the rod called that connects the piston to the driving wheels?
87386.e: The main rod works like a connecting rod. It turns the back and forth movement of the steam piston into the rotation of the wheels.
87386.m: On a steam locomotive the connecting rod is called the main rod.

87387.q: How many connecting rods does an inline four-cylinder engine have?
87387.e: Each cylinder has a piston, and each piston needs its own connecting rod.
87387.m: Every piston has its own connecting rod.

87388.q: What material are connecting rods in car engines usually made of?
87388.e: Connecting rods have to withstand large forces and swing back and forth very often. Forged steel is strong and tough.
87388.m: Connecting rods are usually made of strong steel.

87389.q: What load does a connecting rod have to withstand when the mixture in the cylinder burns?
87389.e: The combustion pushes the piston down with great force. This force is passed through the connecting rod onto the crankshaft.
87389.m: The connecting rod transfers the piston's pressure.

87390.q: How many times does the connecting rod move the piston all the way down when the crankshaft turns once?
87390.e: In one turn of the crankshaft the piston travels once all the way down and once all the way up.
87390.m: Per turn the piston makes one stroke down and one up.

87391.q: A spring has a spring constant of 200 N/m and is stretched by 0.05 m. What force is needed for this?
87391.e: According to Hooke's law, force equals spring constant times extension: 200 N/m × 0.05 m = 10 N.
87391.m: Spring force is spring constant times extension.

87392.q: A spring is stretched by 2 cm by a force. How far does it stretch with twice the force?
87392.e: According to Robert Hooke's law, the extension is proportional to the force. Twice the force means twice the extension.
87392.m: Twice the force stretches a spring twice as far.

87393.q: What unit is the spring constant given in?
87393.e: The spring constant tells you how much force is needed for one metre of extension. That is why it is measured in N/m.
87393.m: The spring constant is measured in newtons per metre.

87394.q: Which spring stores the energy that drives a mechanical wristwatch?
87394.e: The mainspring is a coiled steel band in the barrel. Winding the watch tightens it, and it slowly releases the energy to the movement.
87394.m: In mechanical watches the mainspring drives the movement.

87395.q: Which type of spring is made of several steel strips stacked on top of each other and is used on lorries?
87395.e: Leaf springs are made of layered, slightly curved steel leaves. They carry heavy loads and absorb shocks.
87395.m: Lorries often have leaf springs made of steel strips.

87396.q: What kind of energy is stored in a stretched spring?
87396.e: When you stretch a spring, you do work on it. This work is stored as elastic energy and released again when the spring relaxes.
87396.m: A stretched spring stores elastic energy.

87397.q: What happens if you stretch a steel spring far too much?
87397.e: Beyond the elastic limit the spring no longer returns to its old shape. Then Hooke's law no longer applies either.

87398.q: A spring is stretched by 2 cm with 3 N. How far does it stretch with 6 N if it stays within the elastic range?
87398.e: Force and extension are proportional. Twice the force gives twice the extension: 2 × 2 cm = 4 cm.
87398.m: Twice the force gives twice the extension.

87399.q: Which property of liquids does hydraulics make use of?
87399.e: Because a liquid can hardly be compressed, pressure is passed on immediately and completely.
87399.m: Hydraulics uses the fact that liquids barely compress.

87400.q: Which scientist is the principle named after which says that pressure in a liquid spreads equally in all directions?
87400.e: In the 17th century the Frenchman Blaise Pascal described that pressure in a still liquid acts equally everywhere.
87400.m: Pressure spreads equally everywhere in a liquid.

87401.q: In a hydraulic press the small piston has 2 cm² and the large one 100 cm². You push the small one with 50 N. What force acts on the large one?
87401.e: The area is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 times larger, and so is the force: 50 N × 50 = 2500 N.
87401.m: The force grows in the same ratio as the piston area.

87402.q: How many pascals is a pressure of 1 bar?
87402.e: 1 bar is 100,000 pascals. That is roughly the air pressure at sea level.
87402.m: One bar is a hundred thousand pascals.

87403.q: Which construction machine usually moves its arm with hydraulic cylinders?
87403.e: Excavators have a hydraulic pump and several cylinders. With them they lift the arm and bucket with great force.

87404.q: What do you have to accept with a hydraulic press when the force is increased?
a: A longer distance at the small piston
A lower pressure in the system
87404.e: What you gain in force, you have to make up in distance. The small piston has to be pushed much further than the large one rises.
87404.m: In hydraulics, more force means more distance at the small piston.

87405.q: Which liquid is mostly used in hydraulic systems?
87405.e: Hydraulic oil can hardly be compressed, lubricates the parts and protects against rust.
87405.m: Hydraulic systems mostly work with oil.

87406.q: What is the part called in which liquid pressure pushes a piston out?
87406.e: In a hydraulic cylinder the liquid pushes on a piston. The piston rod extends and moves, for example, a tipping platform.
87406.m: A hydraulic cylinder turns oil pressure into movement.

87407.e: Pneumatic systems move pistons and tools with compressed air.

87408.q: Which device produces the compressed air for a pneumatic system?
87408.e: The compressor sucks in air and presses it into a tank. From there it goes through pipes to the machines.

87409.q: How are the capsules in a pneumatic tube system, for example in hospitals, moved along?
87409.e: A blower creates overpressure or suction in the tube. The air pushes or sucks the capsule through the network of tubes.
87409.m: Pneumatic tube capsules are moved by air.

87410.q: Why can pneumatics hold loads at one spot less precisely than hydraulics?
87410.e: Under load, air gives way like a spring. That is why pneumatic movements are fast but less precise.
87410.m: Air can be compressed and so it springs back.

87411.q: Which vehicles typically brake with air brakes?
87411.e: Heavy vehicles produce their own compressed air on board. The compressed air works the brakes of all wheels or carriages.
87411.m: Lorries and trains brake with compressed air.

87412.q: Why must compressed air be dried before use?
87412.e: When air is compressed, water condenses out of it. It could make pipes and cylinders rust.
87412.m: Compressed air is dried so water cannot cause rust.

87414.q: What is the part called in which compressed air moves a piston back and forth?
87414.e: When compressed air flows into the cylinder, it pushes the piston out. Pneumatic cylinders open doors, for example, or move parts in factories.
87414.m: A pneumatic cylinder moves a piston with compressed air.

87415.q: How do you calculate torque when the force acts at right angles to the lever arm?
87415.e: Torque is the product of the force and the length of the lever arm. A large force or a long arm gives a strong turning effect.
87415.m: Torque is force times lever arm.

87416.q: What unit is torque measured in?
87416.e: Because you multiply newtons by metres, the unit is the newton metre (Nm).
87416.m: Torque is measured in newton metres.

87417.q: You push with 50 N at right angles on the end of a 0.4 m spanner. How big is the torque?
87417.m: Torque is calculated from force and lever arm.

87418.q: A bolt needs 30 Nm of torque. The spanner is 0.2 m long. What force must you apply at right angles?
87418.e: Force = torque divided by lever arm: 30 Nm ÷ 0.2 m = 150 N.
87418.m: With a short spanner you need more force.

87419.q: What is a torque wrench for?
a: To tighten bolts to an exact tightness
87419.e: With a torque wrench you set a specific torque. That way wheel nuts, for example, are tightened neither too loosely nor too tightly.
87419.m: A torque wrench tightens bolts to an exact torque.

87420.q: When is the torque greatest for the same force?
a: When the force acts at right angles to the lever
When the force acts along the lever
When the force points at an angle to the axle
When the force acts on the axle
87420.e: Only the part of the force at right angles to the lever arm causes rotation. If the force acts along the lever, nothing turns.
87420.m: A force turns most strongly at right angles to the lever.

87421.q: Why is it best to push a heavy door open far away from the hinges?
a: Because the lever arm is longest there
Because the door is lighter there
Because there is less friction there
Because the door is thinner there
87421.e: The hinges form the pivot. The further away you push, the greater the torque for the same force.
87421.m: Far from the pivot, a little force is enough.

87422.q: Why do electric cars often accelerate very strongly from a standstill?
a: The electric motor has high torque even at a standstill
The electric motor only turns very slowly
87422.e: An electric motor delivers its greatest torque at very low speeds. A petrol engine first has to rev up for that.
87422.m: Electric motors have lots of torque when pulling away.

87423.q: How does the torque change if you use a spanner twice as long with the same force?
87423.e: The lever arm is twice as long, so the product of force and lever arm is twice as large too.
87423.m: A lever twice as long gives twice the torque.

87424.q: What is the clutch for in a car with a manual gearbox?
a: It disconnects the engine from the gearbox
87424.e: When you press the clutch, the connection between engine and gearbox is broken. Only then can you pull away and change gear.
87424.m: The clutch disconnects the engine from the gearbox when changing gear.

87425.q: Which pedal is furthest to the left in a car with a manual gearbox?
87425.e: The order from left to right is clutch, brake, accelerator. You work the clutch with your left foot.
87425.m: The clutch pedal is furthest to the left.

87426.q: Which type of clutch is most common in cars with a manual gearbox?
87426.e: A clutch plate is pressed between the flywheel and the pressure plate. The friction transfers the power and allows smooth pulling away.
87426.m: Cars usually have a friction clutch.

87427.q: What happens if you let the clutch slip for a long time while driving?
87427.e: When the clutch slips, the surfaces rub against each other. They get hot and the lining wears out faster.
87427.m: Letting the clutch slip wears it out.

87428.q: What does a flexible shaft coupling do?
87428.e: A rubber or plastic part connects the two shafts flexibly. This cushions jolts and makes up for small misalignments.

87429.q: Which clutch on a chainsaw or moped only engages above a certain engine speed?
87429.e: At higher speeds, weights are pushed outwards and press against a drum. That is why the chain stays still when idling.
87429.m: A centrifugal clutch only engages at higher speeds.

87430.q: Which device on a bike lets you roll along without pedalling?
87430.e: The freewheel in the rear hub transmits force in one direction only. If the wheel turns faster than the pedals, it simply runs free.
87430.m: Thanks to the freewheel you can roll along on a bike without pedalling.

87431.q: What does a dual-clutch gearbox have?
a: Two clutches for fast gear changes
Two steering wheels for two drivers
87431.e: One clutch handles the even gears, the other the odd gears. The next gear is preselected, so changing gear happens almost without interruption.
87431.m: A dual-clutch gearbox changes gear very fast thanks to two clutches.

87432.q: Into which form of energy does a friction brake mainly convert movement energy?
87432.e: The brake pads rub on the disc or drum. This turns the movement energy into heat, which is why brakes get hot.
87432.m: Friction brakes turn movement into heat.

87433.q: What do the brake pads press on in a disc brake?
a: A brake disc on the wheel
87433.e: A brake calliper presses the pads against the disc from both sides. The disc turns with the wheel.
87433.m: In a disc brake, pads clamp a disc.

87434.q: How does a drum brake work?
a: Brake shoes press from inside against a drum
A band wraps round the tyre
A block presses on the road
87434.e: A drum brake contains two brake shoes. When braking, they are pressed outwards against the turning drum.
87434.m: In a drum brake, shoes press against a drum from inside.

87435.q: What is the anti-lock braking system (ABS) for?
a: The vehicle can still be steered
The braking distance is always zero
87435.e: ABS stops the wheels from locking during an emergency stop. Wheels that are still turning can still be steered.
87435.m: Thanks to ABS a vehicle can still be steered while braking.

87437.q: Why should you use a lower gear on long descents in the Alps?
a: So the brakes do not overheat
87437.e: In a lower gear the engine helps to brake the vehicle. The wheel brakes are spared and do not overheat.
87437.m: Downhill, use engine braking to spare the brakes.

87438.q: How do you use a coaster brake on a bike?
87438.e: The coaster brake sits in the rear hub. When you pedal backwards, a mechanism presses brake parts against the hub.
87438.m: A coaster brake brakes when you pedal backwards.

87439.q: Which liquid passes the force from the brake pedal to the wheels in a car?
87439.e: The brake pedal pushes on a piston in the master cylinder. The brake fluid passes the pressure through pipes to all the wheels.
87439.m: Brake fluid passes the braking pressure to the wheels.

87440.q: In a belt drive, what connects two pulleys to each other?
87440.e: The belt goes round both pulleys. By friction or teeth it transfers the rotation from one shaft to the other.
87440.m: A belt transfers rotation between two pulleys.

87441.q: Which belt drives the camshaft in many car engines?
87441.e: The timing belt has teeth and does not slip. That way the crankshaft and camshaft always turn exactly in time.
87441.m: The timing belt keeps the camshaft in time.

87442.q: What is the slight slipping of a belt on the pulley called?
87442.e: With smooth belts, the belt lags a little behind the pulley under load. This is called slip.
87442.m: Slip is the slipping of a belt.

87443.q: What shape is the cross-section of a V-belt?
a: Triangular with the point at the top
87443.e: The V-belt is narrower at the bottom than at the top. It wedges into the groove of the pulley and so transfers a lot of force.
87443.m: A V-belt has a trapezium-shaped cross-section.

87444.q: How do two pulleys turn if the belt between them is crossed?
87444.e: With an open belt both pulleys turn the same way. If you cross the belt, the second pulley turns the other way.
87444.m: A crossed belt reverses the direction of rotation.

87445.q: A pulley with a 10 cm diameter turns at 1200 revolutions per minute and drives a pulley with a 30 cm diameter. How fast does that one turn?
87445.e: The large pulley is three times as big and therefore turns three times more slowly: 1200 ÷ 3 = 400.
87445.m: A larger pulley turns more slowly.

87446.q: What advantage does a belt drive have over gears?
87446.e: A belt can connect shafts that are far apart. It runs quietly and absorbs shocks.
87446.m: Belts quietly connect even shafts far apart.

87447.q: What is the pulley called that keeps a belt tight?
87447.e: The tensioner pulley presses against the belt. That way it stays tight and does not slip off the pulleys.
87447.m: A tensioner keeps the belt tight.

87448.q: How were many machines in factories around 1900 often driven by a single power source?
a: By shafts on the ceiling and flat belts
By solar cells on the roof
87448.e: A steam engine or a water wheel turned long line shafts. Wide flat belts led from there to every machine.
87448.m: Line shafts with belts used to drive whole factories.

87549.q: What do you call a single command in a program, for example print("Hoi")?
87549.e: A statement tells the computer what to do next. A program is made of many statements that are carried out one after another.
87549.m: A program is a sequence of statements.

87550.q: What does this Python program print: x = 3, then x = 7, then print(x)?
87550.e: The statements run from top to bottom. The second assignment overwrites the old value 3, so 7 is printed.
87550.m: A new assignment overwrites the old value of a variable.

87551.q: What does this program print: x = 5, then y = x, then x = 2, then print(y)?
87551.e: With y = x, the value at that moment, 5, is stored in y. The later change to x no longer affects y.
87551.m: A variable keeps the value it was given at the assignment.

87552.q: Which symbol assigns a value to a variable in Python?
87552.e: With the equals sign, the value on the right is stored in the variable on the left. So it is best to read x = 5 as “x gets the value 5”.
87552.m: In Python the single equals sign stands for an assignment.

87553.q: What does this program print: a = 2, then b = 3, then a = b, then b = a, then print(a, b)?
87553.e: With a = b, a gets the value 3 and the old value 2 is lost. After that b gets the new value of a, so 3 again.
87553.m: To swap two variables you need a helper variable or a multiple assignment.

87554.q: What does this program print: a = 4, then b = a * 3, then print(b-a)?
87554.e: First b = 4 · 3 = 12. Then 12 minus 4 = 8 is printed.
87554.m: Variables can be used in calculations just like numbers.

87555.q: What does print(7 / 2) print in Python?
87555.e: The operator / divides exactly and gives a decimal number of type float.
87555.m: In Python the single slash always gives a decimal number.

87556.q: What does print(17 % 5) print in Python?
87556.e: The operator % gives the remainder of a division. 17 = 3 · 5 + 2, so the remainder is 2.
87556.m: With the percent sign, Python calculates the remainder of a division.

87557.e: The method count counts how often a piece of text appears. In “Bananen” (German for bananas) the small a appears twice.
87557.m: With count you count how often a character appears in a text.

87558.e: If you multiply a string by a number, it is joined together that many times. No spaces are put in between.
87558.m: A string times a number gives the text repeated.

87559.e: Each character has a number, its index. Counting starts at 0, so index 0 is the B.
87559.m: In Python, counting characters starts at zero.

87560.e: The method replace replaces every occurrence of the first text with the second. Here only the small z is replaced by a capital Z.
87560.m: With replace you swap parts of a text.

87561.e: The method upper turns all letters into capital letters. With lower you get only small letters instead.
87561.m: With upper all letters are written as capitals.

87562.e: The quotation marks turn 3 and 4 into text. The plus sign joins two strings together instead of adding.
87562.m: The plus sign joins strings into a longer text.

87563.e: With in you check whether one text appears in another. “Wal” is at the beginning of “Walensee”, so the result is True.
87563.m: With in you find out whether a piece of text appears in a text.

87564.e: A slice [1:4] takes the characters with index 1, 2 and 3. The character with index 4 is not included.
87564.m: When slicing, the end limit is not included.

87565.q: How do you write a string in Python?
87565.e: Text must be between single or double quotation marks. Without them, Python thinks the word is a variable name.
87565.m: In Python strings are always between quotation marks.

87566.q: What does this program print: zahlen = [4, 8, 15], then print(zahlen[1])?
87566.e: The elements of a list are numbered from 0. So index 1 is the second element, the 8.
87566.m: The second element of a list has the index one.

87567.q: What does this program print: l = [4, 5, 6], then l.pop(), then print(l)?
87567.e: The method pop without an argument removes the last element of the list. 4 and 5 are left.
87567.m: With pop you remove the last element of a list.

87568.q: What does this program print: l = [1, 2], then l.append(5), then print(l)?
87568.e: The method append adds a new element to the end of the list. The existing elements stay.
87568.m: With append you add an element to the end of a list.

87569.q: Which brackets do you use to write a list in Python?
87569.e: A list like [3, 7, 1] is written in square brackets, with the elements separated by commas. Round brackets are needed, for example, for function calls.
87569.m: In Python you write lists with square brackets.

87570.e: The function sum adds up all the numbers in a list. 2 + 4 + 6 makes 12.
87570.m: With sum you add up all the numbers in a list.

87571.e: The function max gives the biggest element of a list. Of 4, 9 and 2, 9 is the biggest number.
87571.m: With max you find the biggest value in a list.

87572.q: What happens with l = [1, 2, 3], then print(l[3])?
87572.e: The list has the indices 0, 1 and 2. Index 3 does not exist, so Python reports an IndexError.
87572.m: The biggest valid index is the length of the list minus one.

87573.q: What does this program print: l = [1, 2, 3], then l[0] = 9, then print(l)?
87573.e: With l[0] = 9 the element at position 0 is replaced. The length of the list stays the same.
87573.m: You can change single elements of a list using their index.

87574.e: The function sorted gives a new list sorted in ascending order. The smallest number is then at the front.
87574.m: With sorted you get a list sorted in ascending order.

87575.q: Which numbers does “for i in range(3): print(i)” print?
87575.e: range(3) starts at 0 and stops before 3. That is why 0, 1 and 2 are printed.
87575.m: The function range starts at zero and ends before the given number.

87576.e: The first number is the start and is included. The second number is the limit and is no longer included.
87576.m: With range the start value is included, the end value is not.

87577.q: Which number does range(0, 10, 2) give last?
87577.e: The third number is the step: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. The 10 is the limit and is not reached.
87577.m: The third value in range sets the step.

87578.q: What does this program print: s = 0, then for i in range(1, 5): s = s + i, then print(s)?
87578.e: The loop adds 1, 2, 3 and 4. Together that makes 10.
87578.m: With a loop you can add up lots of numbers one after another.

87579.q: What does “for b in "Uri": print(b)” print?
a: U, r and i, each on its own line
87579.e: A for loop can go through a string character by character. print adds a line break after each output.
87579.m: A for loop can also go through the characters of a text.

87580.e: The step of -1 counts backwards. The 0 is the limit and is no longer included.
87580.m: With a negative step, range counts backwards.

87581.q: What do you call the variable i in “for i in range(10):”?
87581.e: The loop variable takes the next value on each pass. So it keeps count of which pass the loop is on.
87581.m: The loop variable counts the passes of a counting loop.

87582.q: What does this program print: p = 1, then for i in range(1, 5): p = p * i, then print(p)?
87582.e: The loop multiplies by 1, 2, 3 and 4. That gives 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 = 24.
87582.m: With a loop you can also multiply numbers one after another.

87583.q: What value does i have after “for i in range(7): pass” has finished?
87583.e: range(7) gives 0 to 6. After the last pass, i keeps the last value, 6.
87583.m: The last value of range is one less than the limit.

87584.q: What does this program print: x = 1, then while x < 20: x = x * 2, then print(x)?
87584.e: x is doubled: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. At 32, x < 20 is false, the loop ends and 32 is printed.
87584.m: A while loop checks its condition again before every pass.

87585.q: When does a while loop stop?
87585.e: The while loop runs as long as the condition is true. When it becomes false, the program carries on after the loop.
87585.m: A while loop repeats as long as its condition is met.

87586.q: What does this program print: n = 10, then while n > 0: n = n-3, then print(n)?
87586.e: n becomes 7, 4, 1 and then -2. Only at -2 is n > 0 false, so -2 is printed.
87586.m: A loop can overshoot the intended target.

87587.q: How many times does “i = 0, then while i < 5: i = i + 2” run?
87587.e: i takes the values 0, 2 and 4, then it becomes 6. For 0, 2 and 4 the condition is true, so the loop runs 3 times.
87587.m: With bigger steps a loop needs fewer passes.

87588.q: Which command ends a loop in Python immediately?
87588.e: break jumps straight out of the loop. continue only jumps to the next pass, and pass does nothing at all.
87588.m: With break you leave a loop immediately.

87589.q: How many times is the body of “while 5 < 3:” carried out?
87589.e: The condition 5 < 3 is already false at the first check. That is why the body is not carried out even once.
87589.m: If the condition is false from the start, a while loop does not run at all.

87590.q: What does a loop “while True:” need so that it ends at some point?
87590.e: The condition True is always true. Only a break, carried out for example after a certain input, can end the loop.
87590.m: A loop with while True is usually ended with break.

87591.q: When is a while loop especially suitable?
a: When the number of passes is not known beforehand
When you only want to print one line
When you want to write a comment
87591.e: One example is a guessing game that keeps asking until the number is guessed. Nobody knows beforehand how many tries it will take.
87591.m: The while loop is suitable when you do not know how often it has to repeat.

87592.q: What does the command continue do in a loop?
a: It jumps straight to the next pass
87592.e: The remaining statements of the current pass are skipped. After that it carries on with the next pass.
87592.m: With continue you skip the rest of a loop pass.

87593.q: Which operator do you use in Python to check whether two values are equal?
87593.e: The double equals sign compares two values and gives True or False. So 3 == 3 gives the value True.
87593.m: To check for equality you need two equals signs.

87594.q: Which operator means “not equal to” in Python?
87594.e: The exclamation mark stands for “not”. So 4 != 5 gives True.
87594.m: In Python you check for inequality with an exclamation mark and an equals sign.

87595.e: The operator >= means “greater than or equal to”. Since 7 equals 7, the comparison is true.
87595.m: Greater than or equal to is also true when both values are the same.

87596.e: 3 is not greater than 5. A comparison always gives a truth value, here False.
87596.m: A comparison always gives True or False.

87597.e: Python distinguishes between capital and small letters. “A” and “a” are different characters, so the words are not equal.
87597.m: When comparing texts, capital and small letters matter too.

87598.q: What data type does the result of a comparison like 4 < 9 have?
87598.e: A comparison gives True or False. These truth values have the data type bool, named after the mathematician George Boole.
87598.m: Truth values have the data type bool in Python.

87599.q: What does this program output: x = 12, then print(10 < x < 15)?
87599.e: Python allows chained comparisons. 10 < 12 and 12 < 15 are both true, so the result is True.
87599.m: In Python you can check whether a number lies between two limits.

87600.e: On the left is the string “5”, on the right the number 5. For Python, text and a number are not equal.
87600.m: A number in quotation marks is text, not a number.

87601.q: What does print(True and False) output?
87601.e: and is only true if both sides are true. Here one side is false, so the result is False.
87601.m: An and expression is false as soon as one side is false.

87602.q: What does print(True or False) output?
87602.e: or is true as soon as at least one side is true. Here the left side is true.
87602.m: With or it is enough for one condition to be met.

87603.e: not reverses a truth value. True becomes False and False becomes True.
87603.m: The operator not flips a truth value.

87604.q: What does this program output: x = 8, then print(x > 5 and x < 10)?
87604.e: 8 > 5 is true and 8 < 10 is also true. Because both parts are true, and gives True.
87604.m: With and you can check whether a number lies within a range.

87605.q: What does this program output: age = 12, then print(age < 6 or age > 65)?
87605.e: 12 < 6 is false and 12 > 65 is also false. Because neither side is true, or gives False.
87605.m: In an or expression you check each side separately.

87606.e: not (3 > 5) gives True, because 3 > 5 is false. But 2 < 1 is false, and True and False gives False.
87606.m: In longer expressions you work out the brackets first.

87607.q: How many rows does a truth table for two truth values a and b have?
87607.e: Each value can be True or False. That gives 2 · 2 = 4 possible combinations.
87607.m: With every extra variable, the number of rows in a truth table doubles.

87608.q: What does print(True or False and False) output?
87608.e: and is evaluated before or, a bit like multiplication before addition. First False and False gives False, then True or False gives True.

87609.q: Which command makes the Python turtle move 100 steps forward?
87609.e: The command forward moves the turtle in the direction it is facing and draws a line as it goes. backward moves it backwards.
87609.m: With forward the turtle walks forwards.

87610.q: What does the turtle command left(90) do?
a: It turns the turtle 90 degrees to the left
It moves the turtle 90 steps to the left
It draws a circle with radius 90
It puts the turtle at the left edge
87610.e: left turns the turtle on the spot by the given number of degrees. No line is drawn.
87610.m: With left and right the turtle turns without moving.

87611.q: Which command makes the Python turtle draw its lines in red?
87611.e: The command pencolor sets the colour of the pen. All lines drawn afterwards appear in this colour.
87611.m: With pencolor you choose the turtle's pen colour.

87612.q: Where does the Python turtle move with the command goto(0, 0)?
a: To the centre of the window
87612.e: The turtle works with a coordinate system whose origin (0, 0) is in the centre of the window. That is also where it starts when the program begins.
87612.m: For the turtle, the point with coordinates zero and zero is in the centre of the window.

87613.q: What does the turtle command penup() do?
87613.e: penup lifts the pen. Only after pendown does the turtle draw lines again.
87613.m: With the pen lifted, the turtle can jump without leaving a trail.

87614.q: What is the turtle in Python turtle graphics?
a: A figure that draws lines as it moves
87614.e: The turtle is a small figure on the screen. You give it commands such as forward or left, and it draws its path as a line.
87614.m: The turtle draws lines on the screen with its path.

87615.q: Which shape does “for i in range(5): forward(100); right(144)” draw?
87615.e: At 144 degrees the turtle turns so sharply that the lines cross. After 5 lines it has turned all the way round twice (720 degrees) and is back at the start.
87615.m: A large turning angle creates star-shaped figures.

87616.q: What does the turtle command circle(50) draw?
87616.e: The number gives the radius. So the circle has a diameter of 100 steps.
87616.m: With circle, the number gives the radius of the circle.

87617.q: Which numbers can random.randint(1, 6) return in Python?
87617.e: With randint both limits are included. This lets you simulate a normal dice.
87617.m: With randint both limits are possible results.

87618.q: Which module do you need to import in Python to create random numbers?
87618.e: With import random, functions such as randint, choice and shuffle become available. The math module, on the other hand, contains mathematical functions such as sqrt.
87618.m: In Python, random functions are found in the random module.

a: A randomly chosen element of the list
87619.e: choice picks a single element from a list at random. This lets the computer play “rock, paper, scissors”.
87619.m: With choice the computer picks a random element from a list.

87620.q: What are random numbers called that a computer creates with a calculation rule?
87620.e: A computer works by fixed rules and cannot really roll a dice. Its numbers only seem random, which is why they are called pseudorandom numbers.
87620.m: Computers usually create numbers that only seem random.

87621.q: Why does a dice game on the computer need random numbers?
a: So that the same number is not rolled every time
So that the computer starts faster
So that the game uses less electricity
So that the screen gets brighter
87621.e: With random numbers, for example from random.randint(1, 6), every roll gives a different score. This keeps the game exciting.
87621.m: Random numbers make sure a game does not always go the same way.

87622.q: In which range does a number from random.random() lie?
87622.e: random.random returns a decimal number that is at least 0 and less than 1. By multiplying you can make the range bigger.
87622.m: The function random returns decimal numbers between zero and one.

87623.q: What is the probability that random.randint(1, 4) returns the number 4?
87623.e: There are 4 equally likely results: 1, 2, 3 and 4. One of them is 4, so 1 in 4 or 25 per cent.
87623.m: With equally likely results you divide one by the number of possibilities.

87624.q: A program rolls a dice 600 times with randint(1, 6). Roughly how often would you expect a 6?
87624.e: Each number has a probability of 1/6. 600 divided by 6 is 100, but the exact result varies.
87624.m: With many attempts, the frequency gets close to the probability.

87625.q: Which Python function reads input from the keyboard?
87625.e: input waits until the user types something and presses Enter. print, on the other hand, is responsible for output.
87625.m: With input a program asks for something from the keyboard.

87626.q: Which data type does input() always return in Python?
87626.e: Even if you type a number, input returns text. If you want to calculate, you have to convert the text first.
87626.m: The function input always returns text.

87627.q: What does int() do in the line age = int(input("Age? "))?
a: It converts the text entered into a whole number
It checks whether the age is correct
It shows the age on the screen
87627.e: input returns, for example, the text “12”. int turns it into the number 12, which you can calculate with.
87627.m: With int you turn text into a whole number.

87628.q: With a = input() someone types 5. What does print(a + a) output afterwards?
87628.e: a contains the text “5” and not the number 5. Two texts joined with + are stuck together, so you get 55.
87628.m: You have to convert input before you calculate with it.

a: A and B on two lines
87629.e: If you give print several values separated by commas, Python separates them with a space in the output.
87629.m: Several values in print are output separated by a space.

87630.q: What does end="" do in print("Hello", end="")?
87630.e: Normally a new line starts after every print. With end="" the next output continues on the same line.
87630.m: With end you can decide what follows an output.

87631.q: What does the IPO model stand for in computing?
87631.e: Many programs work in this pattern: they take in data, process it and show a result. A calculator is a simple example.
87631.m: Many programs follow the pattern of input, processing and output.

87632.e: Because of the quotation marks, “3 + 4” is text. Python outputs it exactly as it is and does not calculate.
87632.m: Whatever is in quotation marks is not calculated.

a: Breaking the writing rules of the programming language
An error caused by a missing internet connection
87633.e: Syntax is the grammar of a programming language. If you break it, Python cannot understand the program.
87633.m: A syntax error is a grammar mistake in the program code.

87634.q: What is missing from the line “if x > 3” in Python?
87634.e: After if, for, while and def, Python requires a colon. The indented instructions follow after it.
87634.m: In Python an if condition is followed by a colon.

87635.q: A program runs without an error message but calculates the average wrongly. What is this kind of error called?
87635.e: The program follows all the writing rules but does not do what you want. Python cannot find logic errors like this by itself.
87635.m: You can only find logic errors by testing the results.

87636.q: Which error message appears for print(Hello) if there is no variable called Hello?
87636.e: Without quotation marks, Python looks for a variable called Hello. Because it does not exist, it reports a NameError.
87636.m: Without quotation marks, Python thinks a word is a name.

87637.q: Which error message does Python show for wrong indentation?
87637.e: Indentation means the space at the start of a line. This error happens, for example, if the line after an if condition is not indented.
87637.m: Wrong indentation leads to an IndentationError in Python.

87638.q: Why does Print("Hi") with a capital P not work?
a: Python distinguishes between capital and small letters
Print needs two pairs of brackets
Hi is not an allowed word
Python does not know capital letters
87638.e: The command is print with a small p. For Python, Print and print are two different names.
87638.m: In Python, capital and small letters matter.

87639.q: There is a syntax error in line 10 of a Python program. What happens when you start it?
a: The program does not start at all
Lines 1 to 9 run, then it stops
87639.e: Before running, Python checks the whole code against the writing rules. If it finds a syntax error, not a single line is run.
87639.m: A syntax error stops a Python program from even starting.

87640.q: What is wrong with the Python line “5 = x”?
a: The variable must be on the left of the equals sign
x must be a capital letter
87640.e: In an assignment, the name is on the left and the value on the right. You cannot assign anything to a number, so Python reports a syntax error.
87640.m: In an assignment, the variable name is always on the left.

87641.q: Which character starts a comment in Python?
87641.e: Everything after the # up to the end of the line belongs to the comment. The character is also called a hash.
87641.m: In Python, the hash sign starts a comment.

87642.q: What does Python do with a comment when running a program?
a: It shows it on the screen
It stores it in a variable
87642.e: Comments are only meant for people. The computer skips them completely when running.
87642.m: Comments are skipped when a program runs.

87643.q: Why do people write comments in a program?
a: To explain the code to people
87643.e: Comments help others and yourself to understand the code later. Good comments mainly explain why something is done.
87643.m: Good comments make a program easier to understand.

87644.q: What does the line print("Hi")  # greeting output?
87644.e: The part from # onwards is a comment and is ignored. Only the text in the quotation marks is output.
87644.m: A comment can also be at the end of a line of code.

87645.q: What is it called when you temporarily switch off a line of code with #?
87645.e: When you comment code out, it stays in the program but is not run. This lets you switch off parts for testing without deleting them.
87645.m: By commenting out, you can switch off code without deleting it.

87646.q: Which characters start a single-line comment in JavaScript?
87646.e: In JavaScript, Java and C a single-line comment starts with two slashes. Every programming language has its own rules for this.
87646.m: Different programming languages mark comments in different ways.

87647.q: How do you often write a multi-line explanation in Python, for example at the start of a function?
a: With three quotation marks at the start and end
With a # at the end of each line
87647.e: Text like this is called a docstring. It goes between three quotation marks and may run over several lines.
87647.m: Docstrings go between three quotation marks.

87648.e: Here the # is inside a string. There it is a completely normal character and does not start a comment.
87648.m: Inside quotation marks the hash sign is not a comment.

87649.q: What does a thick cushion of moss feel like when you touch it?
87649.e: Lots of tiny moss plants grow close together. Together they form a soft, springy cushion.
87649.m: A moss cushion is soft like a pillow.

87650.q: What is a cushion of moss made of?
87650.e: A moss cushion is not one single thing. It is made of hundreds of tiny plants standing close together.
87650.m: A moss cushion is made of lots of tiny plants.

87651.q: How tall do most moss plants grow?
87651.e: Mosses stay small. Most of the plants are only a few centimetres tall and grow close to the ground.
87651.m: Moss plants are usually only a few centimetres tall.

87652.q: Where do moss cushions especially like to grow?
a: In the middle of dry sand
87652.e: Mosses need lots of moisture. That is why you often find them in shady forests, by streams and on damp stones.

87653.e: Mosses make no flowers and no seeds. They are green but never flower.

87654.q: Which tiny creatures often live in moss cushions?
87654.e: Water bears, also called tardigrades, are only about half a millimetre long. They find shelter and food in damp moss.
87654.m: Tiny water bears live in moss.

87655.q: What do many birds collect moss for?
87655.e: Moss is soft and keeps things warm. Many birds use it to line their nests.
87655.m: Birds like to line their nests with moss.

87656.q: Where can you often spot moss in a town?
a: In the cracks between paving stones
87656.e: Between paving stones it stays damp for a long time. Moss feels at home there, even in the middle of town.
87656.m: Moss even grows between paving stones.

87657.q: What does a moss cushion do when it rains?
a: It soaks up the water like a sponge
It lets the water run off at once
It becomes as hard as wood
87657.e: Mosses take up rainwater with their whole surface. They act like a sponge.
87657.m: Moss soaks up water like a sponge.

87658.q: What does moss do with the stored water after the rain?
a: It uses it all up in a minute
87658.e: Moss holds the water and releases it bit by bit into the ground. This keeps the forest floor damp for longer.

87659.q: What does a moss cushion look like when it has not rained for a long time?
87659.e: Without water, moss dries out and turns brownish. But often it is not dead.
87659.m: Dry moss looks brown but is often still alive.

87660.q: What happens to dried-out moss when it rains again?
a: It turns green and fresh again
It crumbles to dust at once
87660.e: Many mosses can survive long dry spells. As soon as they get water, they turn green again and carry on growing.
87660.m: After rain, dry moss turns green again.

87661.q: How does moss help in the forest during heavy rain?
a: It holds back lots of water
It sends the water into the air
It makes the ground rock hard
It makes the rain fall faster
87661.e: Moss cushions hold on to lots of rainwater. So less water runs off at once, and the soil is not washed away so easily.
87661.m: Moss holds back lots of rainwater in the forest.

87662.q: Why does the ground under a moss cushion stay damp for a long time?
a: The moss covers it and stores water
It rains more often under moss
